NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)  
The intervention is to apply a graded intergranular glass phase in the seal to reduce differential stress during thermal cycling. Standard practice uses a uniform glass-ceramic seal (15% glass phase), which develops high stress at sharp interfaces due to mismatched CTE. The mitigation replaces this with a bilayer seal: a 5% glass-phase layer adjacent to the anode (lower CTE match) and a 25% glass-phase layer adjacent to the cathode (higher CTE match), creating a smooth CTE transition. This departs from adjacent techniques like graded seals in nuclear reactors, which use continuous gradients (requiring custom fabrication), whereas ours uses a discrete bilayer of procurable stock materials. The bilayer reduces peak stress by distributing strain across the interface, mitigating microcrack initiation.

PHYSICS CHECK  
The governing relation is thermal stress σ ≈ E·α·ΔT / (1–ν), where E is Young’s modulus, α is CTE, ΔT is temperature change, and ν is Poisson’s ratio. For ΔT = 775 K (25°C to 800°C), a uniform seal (α ≈ 9 ppm/K) with an anode (α ≈ 12 ppm/K) induces σ ≈ 150 MPa. The bilayer reduces the effective α mismatch: the 5% layer (α ≈ 10.5 ppm/K) matches the anode better, while the 25% layer (α ≈ 8.5 ppm/K) matches the cathode (α ≈ 10 ppm/K). This lowers the peak Δα to 1.5 ppm/K, reducing σ by ~50% to 75 MPa—below the fracture strength (~100 MPa for glass-ceramics).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
| Component | Class | Description |  
|----------|-------|-------------|  
| Glass-ceramic powder, 5% glass phase | (b) | Commercial glass-ceramic powder (e.g., G18 composition, 5% intergranular phase), applied as a 50-µm layer adjacent to the anode |  
| Glass-ceramic powder, 25% glass phase | (b) | Commercial glass-ceramic powder (e.g., G18 composition, 25% intergranular phase), applied as a 50-µm layer adjacent to the cathode |  
| Standard lamination press | (a) | Existing stack-press equipment, used at standard 800°C/5 MPa conditions for both layers |  
| Standard sintering profile | (c) | Heat to 850°C at 5°C/min, hold 1 hour, cool at 3°C/min (unchanged from standard practice) |  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
| Standard Practice | Proposed Intervention | Burden |  
|-------------------|----------------------|--------|  
| Uniform 15% glass-ceramic seal | Bilayer seal (5% + 25% layers) | Same: two layers applied identically to standard lamination |  
| Single sintering step | Single sintering step (same profile) | Same: no new equipment or process steps |  
| No mass change | Bilayer adds negligible mass (<0.5%) | Same: within 2% constraint |  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Cycle 5 test stacks (3 with bilayer, 2 control) between 25°C and 800°C at 5°C/min, holding 1 hour at each extreme. Measure open-circuit voltage (OCV) and seal leakage (via helium tracer) every 50 cycles.  
Pass/Fail: OCV > 1.0 V and leakage < 1% fuel flow after 500 cycles. Failure if any stack drops below OCV 1.0 V or exceeds leakage.  
Kill Criterion: Stop if 2/3 bilayer stacks fail or if leakage increases by >50% vs. control.  
Duration: 500 cycles (≈2 weeks at 10 cycles/day).
